questions.prompt: Mara keeps refining the research deck but will not draft the proposal itself. In Book One, what makes that pattern Resistance rather than ordinary caution?
choices: The delay gathers around the exact step that would make the work real and exposed
The project is difficult enough that waiting becomes the most responsible choice
The careful prep proves the work is still in its proper early stage

explanation.gentle: Book One becomes suspicious when sensible-looking delay appears at the threshold where commitment should happen.
explanation.direct: Resistance is not just waiting. It is patterned postponement around meaningful action, especially when support work keeps replacing the exposed step.
explanation.competitive: The tell is timing. The smartest delay shows up right where the real move would start.

questions.prompt: Why does Book One treat the blank page as heavier than a pile of small admin tasks?
choices: The blank page requires more technical skill than ordinary tasks
The blank page can turn a private dream into work that other people may judge
The blank page always signals that the project lacks enough research

explanation.gentle: Small tasks may take time, but the blank page carries the extra risk of exposure.
explanation.direct: Meaningful work feels heavier because embodiment creates the chance of judgment, rejection, or disappointment.
explanation.competitive: Admin work can be finished and forgotten. The blank page can hand your fantasy a verdict.

questions.prompt: Which response fits the chapter's treatment of fear most accurately?
choices: Fear can signal that the work matters rather than that it should be avoided
Fear means the project is a poor fit and should be dropped
Fear disappears once Resistance has been named

explanation.gentle: The chapter treats fear as part of the clustered pressure around meaningful work, not as an automatic stop sign.
explanation.direct: Fear belongs to Resistance's architecture because exposure is costly. Naming the pattern changes interpretation, not the raw fact that fear can appear.
explanation.competitive: The flare often rises around the real calling. That makes fear a clue before it becomes an excuse.

questions.prompt: Mara keeps refining the deck around her proposal instead of drafting the proposal itself. Which reading matches Book One?
choices: She is wisely waiting until the project feels fully safe
The surrounding work may have become respectable cover for avoiding commitment
Her problem is mainly that she needs a better software tool

explanation.gentle: The chapter asks whether useful-looking work has started replacing the move that would make the project real.
explanation.direct: Research and polish can be legitimate, but they become suspicious when they repeatedly stand in for commitment at the threshold of exposure.
explanation.competitive: Busy is not the same as brave. Mara's pattern points to cover, not progress.

questions.prompt: Theo says he should wait one more week because the voice of his story is still settling. What trap is the chapter most alert to here?
choices: That all revision is fake
That polished language can hide threshold delay
That workshop feedback always weakens original work

explanation.gentle: The line may contain some truth, but Book One pays attention to when that kind of truth appears.
explanation.direct: Resistance often uses half-reasonable explanations. The timing becomes revealing when refinement only matters at the point of submission.
explanation.competitive: A tasteful excuse is still an excuse if it always shows up right where judgment begins.

questions.prompt: Which statement would overreach the chapter's actual claim?
choices: Resistance helps explain patterned delay around meaningful work
Every difficult or exhausted day should be treated as Resistance in disguise
Rationalization can be one tactic inside a larger pattern

explanation.gentle: The section is strong because it stays specific. It does not claim total authority over every struggle.
explanation.direct: Book One offers a sharp recognition frame, not a complete theory of grief, exhaustion, or structural difficulty.
explanation.competitive: Explaining everything is how a sharp concept turns dull and dishonest.

questions.prompt: In rehearsal, Priya keeps delaying the solo that matters most while finishing smaller assignments easily. What does that pattern suggest?
choices: The solo is objectively too advanced for her to attempt
Meaningful work can attract heavier pushback than low-stakes work
She should focus only on chores because they build confidence

explanation.gentle: Book One expects Resistance to intensify around the work carrying more identity and exposure.
explanation.direct: Low-stakes tasks often move cleanly because little self-risk hangs on them. Central work carries more threat of judgment.
explanation.competitive: The easiest chores are not the point. The real signal is what turns sticky when the work could actually count.

questions.prompt: Janelle keeps the song private because the version in her head still feels perfect. According to the chapter, what is the hidden payoff of that delay?
choices: It protects the imagined version from being tested in reality
It proves she respects the craft more than other musicians do
It guarantees the final version will be stronger later

explanation.gentle: The private version stays safe from judgment as long as it never becomes an actual recording.
explanation.direct: Resistance protects possibility by blocking embodiment. The unfinished state shelters the dream from verdict.
explanation.competitive: No file means no loss, which is exactly why the fantasy can keep feeling grand.

questions.prompt: Why does naming Resistance change leverage even before anyone has become disciplined enough to beat it?
choices: Because awareness automatically removes fear
Because the reader can stop treating each smart excuse as an innocent new event
Because naming the enemy instantly creates confidence

explanation.gentle: The chapter's first win is recognition. Once the pattern is visible, excuses lose some of their innocence.
explanation.direct: Diagnosis changes interpretation. Delay, fear, and rationalization stop traveling as isolated episodes and start reading as tactics in one repeated struggle.
explanation.competitive: You have not won the war yet, but the disguise has taken a hit and that changes the field.

questions.prompt: If Book One names the enemy well, what pressure naturally pushes into Book Two?
choices: How to build a posture that works under Resistance instead of bargaining with it
How to prove that fear is only an illusion
How to replace creative work with safer routines

explanation.gentle: The chapter ends with a tactical question. Awareness helps, but a way of working is still missing.
explanation.direct: Once the pattern is recognized, the next problem becomes practical: what disciplined stance can survive recurring pushback?
explanation.competitive: Naming the enemy removes innocence. Book Two has to remove amateur waiting.
